diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\omega$ be a vertically closed $(p-1,2)$-form on the space $\mathbb{Z}^p\times U$ with $U\subset \mathbb{R}^q$
For a general variational problem, its multisymplectic form may be defined on the total prolongation space.

issues.failure_explanation: The converse passage introduces an arbitrary vertically closed (p-1,2)-form omega (with d_h^Delta omega = 0 on solutions of a first-order PΔE system) and asserts that in coordinates it can be written in the special standard form (eq:multiform): a sum over i of S_i^{-1}(f^i_{αβ}(n,u)) dv(S_i^{-1}u^α) ∧ dv u^β ∧ (∂_{n^i}⌟vol), with coefficients depending only on unshifted (n,u) and vertical one-forms only in the specific shifted/unshifted pairs attached to the horizontal block ∂_{n^i}⌟vol. By the paper's own definition of (k,l)-forms (eq:klform), a general vertically closed (p-1,2)-form may contain vertical parts dv u^α_J ∧ dv u^β_K with arbitrary multi-indices J,K. Counterexample: for p=2, q=2, omega = c·dv u^1_{(0,5)} ∧ dv u^2_{(0,0)} ∧ (∂_{n^1}⌟vol) with constant c≠0 is vertically closed (constant coefficients) but is not of the form (eq:multiform), since the basis elements dv u^α_J ∧ dv u^β_K ∧ (∂_{n^i}⌟vol) are linearly independent and the index pattern (0,5),(0,0) is not the required (-1_i,0) pattern paired with direction i. The asserted coordinate form is therefore false, and the subsequent extraction of conserved standard kappa^i from an arbitrary omega is unproven.

failure_location.quote: In coordinates, the $(p-1,2)$-form $\omega$ can be written as

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the converse claim to vertically closed (p-1,2)-forms already of standard type (the shape of (eq:multiform)/(kap)) and derive the multisymplecticity conclusion from the definition rather than from the normal-form reduction; a genuine reduction of arbitrary closed forms to standard ones would otherwise be required, and no such argument exists in the source.
issues.overall_effect: The converse direction of the multisymplecticity discussion — obtaining conserved standard (0,2)-forms kappa^i from a general vertically closed omega with d_h^Delta omega = 0 on solutions — is not established. The concluding sentence 'This implies the multisymplecticity of the system' survives only trivially (by the paper's definition), not through the exhibited standard conservation laws. Lagrangian-derived forms (e.g. via (olol)) and the examples are standard-type and unaffected.
issues.title: False normal-form claim: general vertically closed (p-1,2)-forms need not have the standard form (eq:multiform)
issues.why_classification: The correction necessarily narrows the stated converse (from all vertically closed forms to standard forms), withdrawing a substantive universality claim, but leaves a recognizably comparable result and does not affect the Lagrangian-based theory — a limited weakening, hence moderate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now we are going to propose a systematic method, with which one can proceed from a multisymplectic structure to an equivalent difference Lagrangian structure.

Khavkine \cite{Khavkine} used this observation to prove the existence of a Lagrangian $(p,0)$-form on the full jet space, whose Euler--Lagrange equations are solved by the given multisymplectic system of PDEs.
Conversely, for a linear system of P$\Delta$Es, if there is a vertically closed $(p-1,2)$-form $\omega$ satisfying $\dDh\!\omega=0$, then there exists a Lagrangian of the form (\ref{lp}).

issues.failure_explanation: The passage claims a systematic method producing a Lagrangian from a multisymplectic structure and concludes that a (p,0)-form L with d_h^Delta eta = dv L on all solutions exists. The inference 'This implies the existence (locally) of a (p,0)-form L' requires vertical exactness of the restricted, on-shell complex on the solution set of the PΔE system, because dv(d_h^Delta eta) = 0 holds only on solutions. The paper's vertical exactness (thm:added-2) is proved only on the free prolongation space, where d_h^Delta eta need not be vertically closed; no argument or citation establishes the on-shell statement. In the differential case the paper itself treats the analogous existence as a nontrivial theorem of Khavkine (cited there), but no difference-case counterpart is provided. The further claim that a linear system admitting a vertically closed omega with d_h^Delta omega = 0 possesses a Lagrangian of the form (lp) is asserted with no proof, and 'equivalent difference Lagrangian structure' overstates even the intended conclusion (the paper's own differential-case caveat says the resulting Euler–Lagrange equations may be weaker than the given system).

failure_location.quote: This implies the existence (locally) of a $(p,0)$-form $\msL$, such that on all solutions $\dDh\!\eta=\dv \!\msL$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove the needed on-shell vertical exactness / Lagrangian existence (the difference-case analogue of the cited result of Khavkine, at least for linear systems), or recast the passage as a conditional or heuristic construction and weaken 'equivalent' to match the differential-case caveat; the unproved linear-system existence claim must be proved or withdrawn.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed construction of a Lagrangian form from a multisymplectic structure, and the linear-system Lagrangian-existence claim, are unsupported; the conclusion that 'the (p,0)-form L is a Lagrangian form for the system of PΔEs' does not follow from the given reasoning. The multimomentum-map framework and Theorem thm:added-1, which start from a given Lagrangian, are not directly affected.
issues.title: Multisymplectic-to-Lagrangian 'systematic method' rests on an unestablished on-shell exactness step
issues.why_classification: A substantive claimed existence result must be supported by a contained but nontrivial new argument or withdrawn/weakened to a conditional statement; since the downstream theory (multimomentum maps, examples) does not depend on it, the loss is limited — moderate rather than serious, but well beyond a routine local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As $\mcI^{\vartriangle}$ is a projection and the difference variational bicomplex is exact, a difference version of equality \eqref{eq:ii} holds.

issues.failure_explanation: Exactness of the augmented horizontal row at Omega^{p,l} — ker(I^Delta) = im(d_h^Delta) — is the central content of Theorem thm:added-3, yet the proof disposes of it in its first sentence as 'an immediate consequence of \eqref{eq:ii}'. The label (eq:ii) is the differential-case identity sigma = I(sigma) - d_h tau; the difference-case analogue is precisely the decomposition the theorem must establish, and the only justification offered for it anywhere in the paper (Section 3) is that 'the difference variational bicomplex is exact', i.e. the theorem itself. The argument is therefore circular (or, read literally, invokes a differential-case result outside its scope), and no independent proof of the top-slot exactness is supplied. The proof of Theorem thm:added-4 reuses the same unestablished identity ('From \eqref{eq:ii}, we have dv sigma = delta_v^Delta sigma + d_h^Delta tau_1').

failure_location.quote: First of all, notice that $\ker (\mcI^{\vartriangle})=\operatorname{im} (\dDh)$, which is an immediate consequence of \eqref{eq:ii}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a non-circular proof of the difference interior-Euler decomposition (equivalently ker(I^Delta) = im(d_h^Delta) on Omega^{p,l}), e.g. the top-slot homotopy argument from the cited thesis [Pe2013], and replace the circular references to (eq:ii) in the proofs of thm:added-3 and thm:added-4.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's foundational exactness theorem for the augmented difference variational bicomplex is not validly proved at the interior-Euler slot. Every result whose proof routes through this exactness inherits the gap: the difference interior-Euler decomposition (eq:dvLag), the coordinate-free Noether conservation law (eq:ddcl, eq:Noecl), Theorem thm:added-1 (its condition (con) is derived from eq:ddcl), and Theorem thm:added-4. Independently verified material (Section 4's symplectic-map computations via vertical exactness; the directly verified eta of Section 5; the examples) is unaffected.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem thm:added-3 assumes the key top-slot exactness circularly via (eq:ii)
issues.why_classification: The theorem's statement is credible and the source (via the thesis citation and the homotopy-operator framework) supports a contained repair that preserves every substantive claim, so neither new global proof architecture nor loss of a result is required; but restoring a valid proof of the paper's central exactness theorem requires a genuine nontrivial argument — moderate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any $\sigma\in\Omega^{k,l}$ with $1\leq k\leq p$, we define the horizontal homotopy operators as

issues.failure_explanation: The identity (eq:hohomo) is asserted for every sigma in Omega^{k,l} with 1 <= k <= p. At k = p it is false: the horizontal one-forms are spanned by Delta^1,...,Delta^p, so any (p+1)-fold horizontal wedge vanishes, Omega^{p+1,l} = 0, and d_h^Delta sigma = 0 for every sigma in Omega^{p,l}; the identity would then read d_h^Delta(h_h^{p,l}(sigma)) = sigma for all sigma in Omega^{p,l}, i.e. d_h^Delta : Omega^{p-1,l} -> Omega^{p,l} would be surjective. But (coch) gives I^Delta d_h^Delta = 0 while I^Delta is not the zero operator (e.g. for p = q = 1, sigma = u_0 dv u_0 ∧ Delta satisfies I^Delta(sigma) = sigma ≠ 0), so such sigma cannot lie in im(d_h^Delta). The identity thus contradicts the paper's own augmentation at k = p. (The formula also involves the undefined operator '(S - id)_I'.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the homotopy identity (eq:hohomo) to 1 <= k <= p - 1, handle the top slot by the interior-Euler argument (see the separate circularity issue), and define the operator '(S - id)_I' (presumably (S - id)_I with S the shift operator).
issues.overall_effect: The stated homotopy identity — the proof's engine for exactness of the horizontal rows — is incorrect as written at k = p, where it would imply the false conclusion that every (p,l)-form is d_h^Delta-exact (equivalently, that the interior Euler operator vanishes on Omega^{p,l}). The statement of Theorem thm:added-3 is not thereby disproved, since the identity is needed (and plausible) only for k <= p - 1, but the proof as presented is unsound at the top degree.
issues.title: Horizontal homotopy identity (eq:hohomo) is false at the top degree k = p
issues.why_classification: The false assertion is confined to the degree k = p, where it is necessarily false and not needed; a one-line restriction of the stated range removes it without losing any true claim or requiring a new argument — minor.
